title: Negative process delta can occur when changing Engine.time_scale + Engine.physics_ticks_per_second
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.5.1 stable and v4.6 rc 1

### System information

Godot v4.6.rc1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.91 GiB memory

### Issue description

When changing both time_scale and physics ticks per second (in order to change the speed of the physics simulation while keeping the same physics delta) to a higher value like so:
```gdscript
Engine.physics_ticks_per_second = speed * 60
Engine.time_scale = speed
```
the delta value used for `_process(delta)` can become negative. This never occurred for me when the `max_physics_steps` project setting was at it's default value, but does so commonly when `max_physics_steps` is set to the minimum 1.

delta becomes negative on this line: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/741fb8a30687d0662ab6b5c04a2a531440dd29d9/main/main.cpp#L4805C3-L4805C16


### Steps to reproduce

Set `time_scale` and `physics_ticks_per_second` to a higher value in `_input`, with the `max_physics_steps` project setting set to 1, and occasionally it will result in a negative delta.

In the provided mrp, just mash num 1 and num 3 a bit.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[negative_delta_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24691827/negative_delta_mrp.zip)
